cutoff_window.date_policy: Only public sources with visible publication, release, merge, or update evidence inside the window were accepted. Missing, future-dated, older, ambiguous, and boundary-only date evidence was excluded.

federation_boundary.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice, workflow, governance, verification, context architecture, adoption, and implementation lens.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Article page and search result show published on September 21, 2026.
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: CloudBees argues that enterprise-scale agentic coding shifts the bottleneck from code generation to review, ownership, spend attribution, pipeline visibility, and evidence of who approved what. It cites survey findings that formal AI-generated-code release processes are not always enforced and frames end-to-end pipeline visibility as the control layer.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local practice implication is that agent output needs delivery-pipeline evidence packages: build, test, scan, reviewer, owner, cost, and approval state should be inspectable together rather than scattered across tools.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Company and product background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps only the pipeline-governance practice implication.

follow_up_notes: Treat survey statistics as vendor-reported unless independently verified.

qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Lockstep separates repository context, task context, reference context, and decision context. It recommends stable repository rules, short task handoffs, live retrieval for reference data, and approved decision records that agents can load by relevance instead of pasting a giant context file.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This reinforces the local context architecture rule that durable instructions, working handoffs, live retrieval, and team decisions are different authorities and should not be collapsed into one long prompt or memory file.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Developer-tool background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps cross-tool continuity practice.
Developer-tool background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps durable context layering practice.
Protocol background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps the reference-context governance lens.

follow_up_notes: Useful contrast: a handoff is temporary task state; approved decision records carry team authority.

qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: HighCircl summarizes a 100-developer study in which participants selected among AI-generated C suggestions with deliberately varied security and functionality. The article reports that only 22 percent of final submissions were fully secure and emphasizes that many developers lacked an explicit security-checking step.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI-assisted review policies should require explicit, structured security checks and not rely on a generic instruction to review AI suggestions. The study is about developer evaluation behavior, not a blanket claim that AI-generated code is less secure than human code.
follow_up_notes: If ingested, cite the underlying preprint directly and preserve the article's caveat about small C tasks and researcher-curated suggestions.

qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub Enterprise Cloud added credential inventory exports for SSH keys, personal access tokens, OAuth app tokens, and GitHub App tokens, including metadata such as scopes, owners, creation and expiration dates, last-used dates, and target organizations or repositories. GitHub says owners can correlate credentials with audit log activity.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent governance depends on knowing which human, app, or connector credentials can touch repositories and tools. Credential inventories are a practical source for incident response, approval review, and delegated-authority audits around coding agents.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Developer platform background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps credential-inventory and audit practice implication.

follow_up_notes: Could be linked from retrieval-and-tools/mcp-scoped-authorization-and-approval-evidence.md as credential evidence outside MCP itself.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub pull request page shows merged Sep 21, 2026 and a Sep 21, 2026 author comment.
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The OpenAI Agents Python SDK merged an optional max_list_pages setting for stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP MCP servers. The PR says automatic tool and prompt listing can otherwise continue fetching successful pages indefinitely when a server returns fresh continuation cursors, including before model execution.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Tool discovery needs deterministic resource bounds. Agent harnesses that enumerate tools or prompts should set page limits and fail with actionable errors instead of allowing unbounded pre-model listing behavior.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Framework background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps governed tool-discovery practice.
Protocol background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps pagination-control practice.

follow_up_notes: Check whether local MCP guidance already says tool/schema discovery must be bounded.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub pull request page shows merged Sep 21, 2026 and a Sep 21, 2026 author comment.
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The OpenAI Agents Python SDK merged a realtime fix so SDK-generated async tool failure events emit fixed messages instead of raw exception details when applications forward events to clients. The PR says original Python exception propagation, cancellation, retries, and opt-in diagnostic logging are preserved.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Streaming progress and realtime tool telemetry should separate user-visible event payloads from internal diagnostic detail. Harnesses need redaction boundaries so tool failures do not leak sensitive exception text to browser clients.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Framework background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps the redacted event-envelope practice.

follow_up_notes: Consider adding a general rule that client-facing agent events should carry safe envelopes and route diagnostics separately.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: GitHub release page shows v0.24.2 released 20 Sep 14:12; this is inside the run cutoff window.
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Qwen Code v0.24.2 release notes include context-file attribution to the extension that loaded each file and its cost, conditional extension rules, capped context warnings, explicit trust for undecided workspaces, internal bwrap-based Linux sandbox foundations, cross-session message judging, and transcript timing surfaces.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Context budgets become governable when each loaded file has provenance and cost. The release also reinforces local practice themes around workspace trust, sandbox foundations, message routing, and transcript timing as harness-level evidence rather than prompt-only behavior.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Developer-tool background belongs upstream; local artifact keeps context attribution, trust, and sandbox practice implications.

follow_up_notes: If ingested, avoid duplicating Qwen Code product coverage and preserve only the practice pattern.
